Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear note and the template. Quick summary up front: we can accept either SEPA (EUR) or CHAPS (GBP). For CHAPS/GBP we have a UK GBP account but we generally invoice in EUR and prefer payments to be sent in the invoiced currency to avoid FX differences — however we can accept GBP where necessary. Below are the recommended instructions and options depending on what your treasury wants.

Option A — Preferred: SEPA (EUR) 
- Bank name: Redwood Treasury N.V. (EUR Nostro)
- IBAN: NL91RDBW0123456789
- SWIFT/BIC: RDBWNL2X
- Instruction: Please send as OUR (sender pays all charges) if possible; if your bank cannot, choose BEN but then include a remittance line showing the gross amount so we can reconcile.
- Notes: SEPA avoids correspondent banks for euro flows inside SEPA zone; intermediary fees are rare.

Option B — CHAPS (GBP) — alternate/accepted
- Bank name: Redwood UK Ltd (GBP Clearing)
- Sort code: 40-72-01
- Account: 12345678
- Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Ltd (please quote INV-2028-137 / DL-8734)
- If your bank sends GBP to our GBP account, your bank will perform FX (at their rate) unless you ask them to send OUR with a currency conversion at their end. We do not perform FX on incoming GBP payments for EUR invoices.

Fee handling guidance (practical):
- OUR = sender covers all intermediary and beneficiary bank charges (full amount reaches us). We ask for OUR if possible.
- BEN = beneficiary pays all intermediary/bene charges (we receive net). If BEN happens, we will reconcile and either request a short payment to make up the delta or apply a one-time recharge on the next invoice.
- SHARED/OUR-net-like: sometimes banks offer "SHA" where fees are split; this often results in small deductions.

VAT and invoices:
- We have attached an updated invoice with the VAT line and a separate payments remit section. For cross-currency payments: please include the exact gross EUR amount and the reference INV-2028-137 in the remittance so we can match the payment even if the bank deducted fees. If you intend to pay GBP, include the EUR gross and the GBP equivalence and the exchange rate used by your bank in the remittance note.

Attachments: redwood_wire_instructions_EUR_GBP.csv (our wire templates + remittance format), updated_invoice_2028-12_DL8734.pdf (VAT line added)

If you want, Laura (cc'd) can approve a temporary concession for this enterprise account on the fee split; Marissa can confirm accounting mechanics for short payments and recharge.

Best,

Hi Oliver — thanks for confirming your treasury preferences. To keep this simple for your team, we can accept CHAPS/GBP to our UK account. Final points: 

1) Fee handling — Redwood policy for this customer (DL-8734): please ask your bank to send as OUR. If that is not possible, we will accept BEN but we will absorb intermediary/correspondent deductions up to 10.00 GBP per payment as a one-time concession for this invoice. Anything above 10 GBP will be recharged via short-pay (Marissa will send the template if needed).

2) FX — if you send GBP, your bank will do the GBP->EUR conversion at their rate. Please include the EUR gross amount in the remittance message and note the FX rate used. We will not perform additional FX conversions on our side for incoming GBP.

3) Remittance/reference — please include INV-2028-137 and DL-8734 in the payment reference and upload a copy of the bank confirmation to payments@stellahealth.com (cc us) so Marissa can reconcile quickly.

4) Attached is the updated invoice with VAT (updated_invoice_2028-12_DL8734.pdf) and a CSV with our wire templates (redwood_wire_instructions_EUR_GBP.csv).

If everything looks good, proceed with CHAPS and confirm the payment date/time; we'll mark the invoice as expected and reconcile when funds arrive.
